correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructed: local vertex-star boundaries are embedded spheres and intersect as the original graph; each extra open-neighborhood simplex attaches along exactly two disjoint contractible faces; girth at least five guarantees that different attachments intersect only inside the previous local-sphere subcomplex. Homotopy pushouts give one new circle per edge, while the local spheres survive integrally. Higher orientations are natural under graph automorphisms. Direct mod-two boundary computations independently reproduce the predicted ranks for Fano, ternary projective plane, Petersen, and mixed-degree Petersen bridge examples. Finite experiments alone are not the general proof.

The mixed-dimensional order-three projective-plane instance is not implied by these results. A semantic and parameter/alias search found no decisive covering statement; nonindexed equivalent work is a residual risk.

value.rationale: Uniform infinite-class homotopy classification: graph cycle rank and vertex degrees separately dictate all global circles and higher sphere dimensions, with integral torsion-free and canonical orientation modules. Applies to all projective-plane incidence graphs and cyclic high-degree irregular graphs, beyond known tree-line-graph and squarefree-graph results. In the ternary projective-plane case 79 circles and 26 two-spheres reveal genuine mixed-dimensional behavior distinct from the closed Čech line-graph invariant.
